source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Stop ciprofloxacin and contact the prescriber promptly; avoid stressing the tendon until evaluated.","B":"Continue ciprofloxacin while temporarily reducing running, and report the problem if swelling or functional limitation develops.","C":"Take each dose with calcium to reduce the risk of tendon rupture.","D":"Finish the course before reporting tendon symptoms unless a rupture occurs."}}
source_row.rationale: Fluoroquinolones, including ciprofloxacin, can cause tendinitis and tendon rupture, sometimes with disabling or irreversible adverse effects. New tendon pain or swelling during therapy warrants stopping the fluoroquinolone and prompt clinical review, with avoidance of exercise or loading of the affected tendon until evaluated.

source_row.stem: An avid runner taking ciprofloxacin develops new Achilles tendon pain and swelling after several doses. Which instruction is most appropriate?
